newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy may slow, recovery to continue-BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy may slow, recovery to continue-BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Friday that Japan's economy may slow temporarily but a recovery is likely to continue.
He said Japan's monetary policy would put emphasis on making the recovery firmer.
He said the effect of the rise in the sales tax on April 1 was appearing strongly and it may be inevitable for the economy to slow temporarily.
Meanwhile, a favourable economic cycle in which rising production leads to growth in incomes and spending was becoming apparent.
Taking this into account, the Japanese economy was likely to overcome the impact of fiscal tightening. "There is a high possibility that the economic recovery will continue," he said.
But he added that the central bank needed to keep watch over consumption and corporate activities to confirm the economic recovery trend.

Meanwhile, price declines had generally come to a halt. Excluding the rise in the sales tax, prices were generally steady. "Our monetary policy will continue to put emphasis on making the basis for economic recovery firmer while keeping close watch on economic developments," he said.
